rationale: Submitted for retained execution the discriminator of the VerifyLeader question: a real four-voter cluster with one voter demoted to nonvoter through the normal DemoteVoter contract, so the configuration has three voters and one nonvoter; the interrupted case partitions the leader together with the nonvoter, and the control partitions the leader on its own. The events separate the applicability of each verification (which suffrages the harness left on the leader's side of the partition) from the outcome (the exported verification's result, the vote tally, and the quorum it was measured against), and the peer-side event records whether the voters the leader cannot reach elected their own leader and committed an entry the interrupted leader never applied, together with the indexes that make that comparison checkable. Native feedback from the local dry run, explicitly not retained evidence: with only the nonvoter on the leader's side the verification returned success with votes 2 against quorum 2, while with no peer at all it returned ErrLeadershipLost with votes 1, and in the first case the two remaining voters elected a leader that committed index 6 while the interrupted leader stayed at applied index 4 - which is why this is worth a retained run rather than a source-only claim.

scope.description: Two trials over real four-voter clusters with the in-memory transport: one voter is demoted to nonvoter with DemoteVoter, the leader is verified while healthy, and then in the interrupted trial the leader is partitioned together with the nonvoter while in the control trial the leader is partitioned alone. Each trial records the verification outcome, the vote tally and the quorum it was measured against, the suffrages on the leader's side of the partition, and - for the interrupted trial - whether the voters the leader cannot reach elected their own leader and committed an entry that the interrupted leader never applied.
assumptions: The in-memory transport is used with the captured in-memory timeouts, so the leader lease and election timers are the same ones the target's own tests use; this keeps the verification inside the window before the interrupted leader's own lease check steps it down.
The demotion goes through the exported DemoteVoter contract, so the configuration that produces three voters plus one nonvoter is produced by the target rather than written into a store by hand.

Reachability is not claimed from the contact timestamps: the leader-side suffrages are a property of the partition the harness applied, reported as such, and the observation that the other voters could not reach the leader is carried by their own election and commit.
Votes and quorum are read through the same in-package accessors the target's own tests use; the verification itself is driven through the same channel the exported VerifyLeader API uses.
excluded: No on-disk store, no network transport and no multi-process execution.
No injection of a synthetic request: every event comes from the target's own leader loop, replication goroutines and exported APIs.

parameters.trials: trial 0 leader partitioned with the nonvoter, trial 1 leader partitioned alone
parameters.cluster: four voters, one demoted to nonvoter after election
parameters.events: verify_baseline (healthy verification), verify_partitioned (verification after the partition, with vote tally and quorum), peer_side (the unreachable voters' new leader and committed entry versus the interrupted leader's applied index)
parameters.recorded_operands: verified, error, votes, quorum_size, leader_state, leader_last_index, partition_leader_side_suffrages, new_leader_elected, write_committed, write_index, leader_applied_index, index_before_partition

comparisons.description: A leader that can exchange RPCs only with a nonvoter is confirmed as leader, with the vote tally reaching the voter quorum.
Control: the same leader with no peer at all is not confirmed, so the confirmation in the other case depends on the nonvoter acknowledgement.

While the interrupted leader holds a successful verification, the voters it cannot reach elect a leader and commit an entry whose index is above the interrupted leader's applied index, so the confirmation is not a valid basis for a consistent read.

experiment.prefix: Each trial builds a real four-voter cluster with MakeCluster and the captured in-memory timeouts, takes the elected leader, and demotes one follower to nonvoter with DemoteVoter, waiting until the leader's configuration shows that server without a vote. It then verifies the healthy leader through the same channel the exported VerifyLeader API uses, recording the outcome, the vote tally the future ended with and the quorum size from quorumSize(), plus how many peers had contacted the leader within the lease and which suffrages the harness is about to leave on the leader's side. It applies one command so the interrupted leader has a known FSM point, applies the partition, and verifies again, recording the same operands and the leader's state. In the interrupted trial it then watches the two voters that the partition detached from the leader until one of them reports Leader, has it commit one entry, and records that entry's index against the interrupted leader's applied index; the control trial stops after the second verification. Only the TestAssurance-prefixed test in this harness is selected and no production file is modified.
